title: Given a list of non-overlapping intervals sorted by start and a new interval to insert, insert the new interval and merge any overlaps so the result remains a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals. Solve it with the three-phase merge-intervals pattern and demonstrate with a complete banking mini-project.
shortTitle: Insert Interval (Insert and Merge into a Sorted Interval List)
keyPoints: Three-phase linear pass: copy intervals before the new one, merge all overlapping intervals, copy intervals after
Input is already sorted and non-overlapping, so no sorting step is needed, giving O(n) time
Merge phase takes the minimum of starts and maximum of ends to absorb overlapping intervals
The new interval can swallow multiple existing intervals in the merge phase
Mid does not advance after a two-swap is the common bug (for DNF), here the common bug is forgetting min-of-starts
Time complexity is O(n), space is O(n) for the result list
This extends the merge-intervals pattern with the sort step already done for us

s1_definition.oneliner: In one pass, copy intervals before the new one, merge all overlapping intervals with the new one, then copy intervals after.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Insert Interval** – insert a new interval into a sorted non-overlapping list and merge any overlaps to keep the list sorted and non-overlapping.
- **Three phases** – (1) copy intervals ending before the new one starts, (2) merge all intervals overlapping the new one into one expanded interval, (3) copy remaining intervals.
- **Merge rule** – take `min(newStart, existingStart)` and `max(newEnd, existingEnd)` for each overlap.
- **Pre-sorted** – the input is already sorted, so no sort step is needed, keeping the solution at O(n).
- **Space** – O(n) for the result list; the input is not mutated.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Rajesh maintains a sorted, non-overlapping schedule of periods when an account is on hold. When a new fraud investigation triggers another hold period, he walks the list once: he keeps every hold that finishes before the new one starts untouched, he fuses the new hold with every hold it bumps into to form one bigger hold, and then he keeps the rest of the holds that begin after the fused hold ends.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Insert Interval: Three-Phase Linear Pass

  Existing: [1,3]  [6,9]  [12,15]
  New:             [5,10]

  Phase 1 (Before): [1,3] ends at 3 < 5 → copy
  Phase 2 (Merge):  [6,9] starts at 6 <= 10 → overlap
                    merged = [min(5,6), max(10,9)] = [5,10]
                    [12,15] starts at 12 > 10 → no overlap
                    → add [5,10]
  Phase 3 (After):  [12,15] → copy

  Result: [1,3]  [5,10]  [12,15]

  ┌─────┐        ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐
  │ 1─3 │        │  5──10    │     │ 12──15   │
  └─────┘        └──────────┘     └──────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The Insert Interval problem gives you an already sorted list of non-overlapping intervals and a new interval, and asks for the sorted non-overlapping list after inserting and merging. Because the input is already sorted, you solve it in a single O(n) pass rather than re-sorting, using three clearly separated phases.

In the first phase you copy every existing interval that ends before the new interval starts, since those lie entirely to the left and cannot overlap. In the second phase you merge every interval whose start is at or before the new interval's end, folding each into the new interval by taking the minimum of the starts and the maximum of the ends. In the third phase you copy the remaining intervals, which all start after the merged interval and cannot overlap.

The details to emphasize are that the merge phase takes the minimum of the starts, not just the maximum of the ends, because the new interval may begin before some overlapping existing interval, and that the merge continues consuming intervals as long as they overlap, because one new interval can swallow several existing ones.

At the National Bank of India, the account-hold system maintained a sorted non-overlapping schedule of hold periods, and whenever a new fraud investigation triggered another hold, the three-phase insert-and-merge kept the schedule clean in a single linear pass.

Remember one sentence: three phases in one linear pass, copy-before, merge-overlaps-with-min-start-and-max-end, copy-after.
